reason: This passage from the Exodus account (the parting of the Red Sea) consistently portrays the Israelites (בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל) as followers of Yahweh in multiple ways: (1) God commands them directly through Moses, and they obey ('Speak to the children of Israel and let them depart'); (2) They follow God's directive to pass through the sea: 'And the children of Israel went into the midst of the sea on the dry ground'; (3) God acts miraculously and exclusively on their behalf while destroying their enemies, establishing a covenant relationship; (4) The narrative structure throughout portrays Yahweh (יְהוָה) as their active leader and protector, with the Israelites as the passive recipients of His commands and salvation. The text explicitly names God as 'Yahweh' (יְהוָה) multiple times as the agent orchestrating their deliverance, leaving no ambiguity about whose God they follow.
story: The Parting of the Red Sea
